cases.exposure_context_quote: A 24-year-old Indian gentleman with no past medical history was brought in by emergency medical services (EMS) with a suspected suicide attempt.
cases.agent: insect killer containing deltamethrin and cypermethrin, 400 mL ingested
cases.agent_quote: History reported by a bystander indicated that the patient had ingested 400 mL of insect killer, which contained deltamethrin and cypermethrin

symptoms.quote: The patient was intubated and sedated, with a heart rate of 180, and the rest of the examination was unremarkable.

symptoms.finding: reduced level of consciousness (GCS 14, dropping to 6 en route)
symptoms.quote: The patient demonstrated a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 14 out of 15 ... en route, his GCS dropped to 6.

symptoms.finding: ST elevation in anterolateral leads with Troponin T rising from 12 to 800; reverse Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (EF 31%)
symptoms.quote: The ECG (Figure 4) monitor showed ST elevation in the anterolateral leads, with an increase in Troponin T from 12 to 800.

symptoms.finding: pulmonary edema on initial chest X-ray; elevated creatine kinase, myoglobin, and troponin
symptoms.quote: Initial chest X-ray (Figure 3) showed increased bronchovascular markings, which were likely due to pulmonary edema ... Initial blood investigations revealed elevated levels of creatine kinase, myoglobin, and troponin

cases.time_to_care: ingested 'just a short while before the crew's arrival' (UNVERIFIED exact interval)

labs.name: Troponin T
labs.quote: The ECG (Figure 4) monitor showed ST elevation in the anterolateral leads, with an increase in Troponin T from 12 to 800.

labs.name: echocardiogram (day 2)
labs.value: EF 31%, global basal hypokinesia, normal apical contractility
labs.quote: an official echocardiogram (Figure 6) was conducted, which showed an ejection fraction (EF) of 31%, with global basal hypokinesia and normal apical contractility, suggestive of reverse Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.

treatment.name: intubation and sedation; skin and eye decontamination
treatment.quote: full personal protective equipment (PPE) was worn, and skin and eye decontamination was performed. The patient was intubated and sedated

treatment.name: supportive management: rehydration, airway/breathing/circulation support (per toxicology)
treatment.quote: they advised supportive management, including rehydration, airway, breathing and circulation support, and neurological vital signs observation.

treatment.name: aspirin and clopidogrel
treatment.quote: They advised continuing medical treatment with aspirin and clopidogrel, with no immediate intervention.

treatment.name: 500 mg bolus of normal saline
treatment.quote: a 500 mg bolus of normal saline was given.

treatment.name: mechanical ventilation with progressive weaning, vasopressors, extubated on day 3
treatment.quote: the patient was more awake and had decreasing mechanical ventilation (MV) settings along with reduced vasopressor requirements. The patient was subsequently extubated.

cases.outcome: survived; returned to baseline and discharged on the seventh day
cases.outcome_quote: On the seventh day of admission, the patient had returned to his baseline and was discharged with regular follow-up planned with cardiology and psychiatry.
cases.notes: Cardiology attributed coronary event to spasm from a metabolic cause, not occlusive coronary artery disease.
